response.title: which enclosed 3d printer makes the strongest nylon parts
response.answer:
For printing the strongest nylon parts, I would prioritize an enclosed 3D printer with an actively heated chamber, rather than simply one with a high nozzle temperature.

The most important factors are:

Chamber temperature: Higher, controlled chamber temperatures improve interlayer bonding and reduce warping.

Nylon compatibility: The printer should reliably handle PA6, PA12, PA-CF, and PA-GF.

Filament drying: Nylon absorbs moisture rapidly, which can significantly reduce print quality and mechanical performance.

Print orientation: Even the best printer produces weaker parts across layer boundaries than along the printed strands.

A key distinction: carbon-fiber-filled nylon is generally stiffer, but not necessarily stronger in every direction than unfilled nylon. If you care about impact resistance or toughness, unfilled PA6 or PA12 may be better.
